title.narrative: Building Mỹ Hải Fund: A Community-Managed Biodiversity Fund to encourage livelihoods alternations toward a healthy and inclusive economy in a beautiful seascape in Vietnam

description.narrative: The Núi Chúa Marine Protected Area (MPA), the marine component of Nui Chua National Park, is a biodiversity hotspot; however, it faces significant threats, which stem from a lack of biodiversity-friendly livelihood alternatives for the local community. Building on decades of experience managing a social fund (Vietnam Bank for Social Policies, Nhon Hai People’s Credit Fund ), this project will establish a biodiversity fund to promote nature-positive, climate-resilient enterprises. The profits generated by the fund will sustainably finance MPA patrol costs. The project will conduct market research to benchmark interest rates of existing loan products, prioritising sectors with tangible biodiversity and social impacts and demonstrated loan demand. FFI will seek legal advice and consult the community to ensure compliance with national law, good governance, and social equity. Co-developing lending rules will prevent unintended consequences and enhance compliance with MPA regulations. FFI will provide financial management and enterprise training to expand fund management capacity beyond village leaders, ensuring borrowers' ability to repay loans. Leveraging FFI's socio-economic study and climate change risk assessments, vulnerable community members will be identified and targeted. The project will establish a robust fund structure with governance, processes, controls, and reporting through a Target Operating Model (TOM). A financial model will assess revenue streams, costs, and funding sources, ensuring the fund's long-term sustainability. The pilot will be scaled by sharing the experience of fund set-up and TOM with another 12 villages and exploring strategic collaborations with other financial service providers in the seascape. The fund will provide finance to pursue at least 30 biodiversity-friendly enterprises as an alternative to illegal unsustainable use. This will directly contribute to the economic development of at least 100 community members and support the conservation of 667ha of MPA core zone.
